import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 233

*References:*
  - [erdosproblems.com/233](https://www.erdosproblems.com/233)
  - [A74741](https://oeis.org/A74741)
  - [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cram%C3%A9r%27s_conjecture)
-/

open Filter Real

namespace Erdos233

/--
A conjecture by Heath-Brown:
The sum of squares of the first $N$ gaps between consecutive primes behaves like $N * (log N)^2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_233 :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^2 := by
  sorry

/--
Cramér proved an upper bound of $O(N(\log N)^4)$ conditional on the Riemann hypothesis.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_233.variants.upper_bound (h : RiemannHypothesis) :
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) =O[atTop] fun N => N * (log N)^4 := by
  sorry

/--
The prime number theorem immediately implies a lower bound of $\gg N(\log N)^2$ for the sum of
squares of gaps between consecutive primes.

Formal proof linked here provided by AlphaProof.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using formal_conjectures at "https://github.com/mzhorvath1/formal-conjectures/blob/032848c62fdf4c422bb0ee6663dc8d009d456c2c/FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/233.lean#L57"]
theorem erdos_233.variants.lower_bound :
    (fun (N : ℕ) => N * (log N)^2) =O[atTop]
    (fun N => ((∑ n ∈ Finset.range N, (primeGap n) ^ 2) : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos233

reformulations.difference: The source sums over 1 ≤ n ≤ N using one-indexed primes; Lean sums over Finset.range N using zero-indexed Nat.nth. The same reindexing occurs in both variants.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Writing p_n = Nat.nth Nat.Prime (n - 1) for n ≥ 1 gives primeGap k = p_{k+2} - p_{k+1}. Thus the Lean sum over k = 0,…,N-1 is exactly the source sum over n = 1,…,N, not merely asymptotically equivalent. Infinitude of the primes makes Nat.nth strictly increasing, so natural-number subtraction introduces no truncation. The pointwise sum identity and the upper-bound equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/checks.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source writes the sum as ≫ N(log N)^2; Lean expresses this by placing N(log N)^2 on the left of =O[atTop].
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Both functions are nonnegative. The reversed big-O statement is equivalent to the existence of c > 0 and N₀ such that c·N(log N)^2 ≤ the sum for every N ≥ N₀. This follows directly from Mathlib's isBigO_iff'' and eventually_atTop, and was proved with the source's one-indexed sum in /workspace/review/checks.lean.

review.notes: All three theorem statements match the Erdős source: the open O(N(log N)^2) conjecture, Cramér's conditional O(N(log N)^4) bound, and the known lower bound. OEIS also records a stronger asymptotic conjecture; that stronger variant is not the claim posed on the Erdős page. Boundary checks verified prime gaps 1, 2, 2, 4 and partial sums 0, 1, 5, 9, 25. The vanishing logarithmic bounds at N = 0 and N = 1 cause no defect because the bounds are eventual. The exact cited lower-bound proof was checked in /workspace/review/proof_audit.lean after adapting only its import and declaration name; its axioms are [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound], with no sorryAx. The reviewed file still matches the specified commit.
